event.tilda_heart5.0.text: Sit a moment, [player]. I baked a dozen scones for a village that buys six.

event.tilda_heart5.1.text: You're eating it without flinching. Felix flinches. He says it's the butter. It isn't the butter.
event.tilda_heart5.1.why: affectionate jab at her oldest friend; player as the good customer

event.tilda_heart5.2.text: Take the mashed potato home, too. I made that for nobody in particular either.
event.tilda_heart5.2.why: matches the item given; admits she cooks for company that never comes

event.tilda_heart2.0.text: Oh, [player]! Just the account I wanted. Come here, I've something to hand over.

event.tilda_heart2.1.text: My mother's cauliflower gratin. She taught it by hand, never wrote it down. Don't thank me. Bring me a cauliflower someday.
event.tilda_heart2.1.why: the gift; she prefers being owed to being thanked

event.hall_dance.3.text: Nobody asked for credit for any of this. So I'm giving it, in the good chalk, under every name in this room.
event.hall_dance.3.why: the slate as the village's memory of the roof

event.hall_dance.10.text: Into the hall box, every coin. Except one. Marcus, that one's for the ladder.
event.hall_dance.10.why: she gives her winnings away and sets up Marcus's dance

event.story_notes_tilda.intro.text: Oh. Oh, it's you. Stand there a moment and look innocent with me.
event.story_notes_tilda.intro.why: caught in the act, recruits the player as accomplice

dlg.story.notes.tilda.0.text: Tilda slides a folded note under a door and straightens up. Neither of you moves.
dlg.story.notes.tilda.0.why: narration of only what the player sees

dlg.story.notes.tilda.1.text: ...Well. Now you know who's been doing it. Not a word to Wren.
dlg.story.notes.tilda.1.why: secret kept from the village's other gossip

dlg.story.notes.tilda.c2.text: Slip a note back. Unsigned, obviously.

dlg.story.notes.tilda.r0.text: ...A smile. No chalk, no receipt. That's the hardest kind to put on a slate.
dlg.story.notes.tilda.r0.why: a smile as a kindness she cannot record

dlg.story.notes.tilda.r1.text: Don't thank me, I'd rather you owed me. ...Oh, now I'm flustered. I'll go rearrange something.
dlg.story.notes.tilda.r1.why: she dislikes thanks; warmth through embarrassment

event.story_notes_tilda.after.text: Signing a kindness is just sending a bill. ...Two more doors before closing. Don't follow me.
event.story_notes_tilda.after.why: why she stays anonymous, in shop terms; a thread

event.story_scarecrows.intro.text: [player]! You're judging. Be completely fair, by which I mean pick mine.

dlg.story.scarecrow.talk.0.text: Mine is smiling. Crows can't stand a cheerful face. That's simply known.

dlg.story.scarecrow.talk.2.text: Well? Whose scarecrow is guarding the fields this fall?

dlg.story.scarecrow.talk.r0.text: Ha! Taste! Take the runner-up home. It'll stand in your field being thoughtful at the crows.
dlg.story.scarecrow.talk.r0.why: gracious winner, ribbing Dorian's quiet scarecrow

dlg.story.scarecrow.talk.r2.text: A tie. Coward. Take one anyway, and we'll both be wounded together.

event.story_scarecrows.after.text: {if choice:scarecrow.tilda}I won. I'm not smug. I'm radiant. Rematch next fall.{else}{if choice:scarecrow.dorian}He won. I'll say it once, quietly. Rematch next fall.{else}{if choice:scarecrow.tie}A tie. I'm not speaking to you, with love. Rematch next fall.{else}The crows chose both. Wise birds. They're on the slate for diplomacy.{/if}{/if}{/if}
event.story_scarecrows.after.why: each outcome lands; a rematch is promised

dlg.story.pumpkin.dorian.1.text: Dorian. Is that my prize pumpkin? I've been blaming the goats all week, out loud!

dlg.story.pumpkin.dorian.r0.text: Kindly, then. But he's on the slate for a pie. Mushrooms optional.

dlg.story.pumpkin.dorian.r2.text: You take the heavy end, Dorian takes the guilt. I'll carry the conversation.

dlg.story.pumpkin.marcus.1.text: Marcus! Is that my prize pumpkin? I blamed the goats. I apologized to a goat.

dlg.story.pumpkin.marcus.r0.text: Kindly. Fine. But he owes me a pie, and I've seen him measure. It'll be exact.
dlg.story.pumpkin.marcus.r0.why: debt plus a joke about the carpenter

dlg.story.pumpkin.marcus.r2.text: You and Marcus take the ends. I'll walk ahead and tell everyone it was the goats.

dlg.story.pumpkin.felix.1.text: Felix. Is that my prize pumpkin? You don't even like vegetables!

dlg.story.pumpkin.felix.r0.text: Kindly. Fine. He owes me a pie, and if there's a fish in it, I'll know.

dlg.story.pumpkin.felix.r2.text: You take the heavy end. Felix can carry the excuses. They weigh more.

event.festival_winter_lanterns.0.text: Lanterns up, everyone. Not lit yet. Wait for the bell. Felix, I mean you.

event.tilda_heart4.intro.text: Come around the counter. Nobody comes back here but me. Mind the cat, it's on duty.

dlg.tilda.slate.0.text: This is the slate. Every small kindness in Wetherell, in chalk. Marcus is two planks ahead of Odalys. She doesn't know yet.

dlg.tilda.slate.1.text: And this blank bit is yours. What shall I write under your name?

dlg.tilda.slate.r0.text: A thank-you. Hard to cash, and I'll never spend it. My favorite currency.

dlg.tilda.slate.r1.text: A joke! On my slate! ...Oh, that's good. Don't tell anyone I laughed in the shop.

dlg.tilda.slate.r2.text: A promise. I'll write it small. I'll hold it large.

event.tilda_heart4.after.text: {if choice:slate.thanks}A thank-you, in chalk. I'll never wipe it, so don't make me.{else}{if choice:slate.joke}A joke on the slate. Nobody's dared. Wren will be furious she didn't think of it.{else}A promise. I hold everyone to everything, kindly. Mostly kindly.{/if}{/if} Now you're on it, you have to come back.
event.tilda_heart4.after.why: closes each branch; debts mean people return

event.tilda_heart6.intro.text: Turn the sign to Closed, would you? Just for an hour. I do the books when it's quiet. Sit.
event.tilda_heart6.intro.why: she makes the quiet herself; the player is the one who sits

dlg.tilda.hours.0.text: I count the stock at closing time. Lately the count comes out right and the street comes out short.
dlg.tilda.hours.0.why: the worry in shop arithmetic, no talk of nights

dlg.tilda.hours.1.text: I tell myself Wetherell isn't shrinking. Then the bell rings twice a day instead of twenty. What do you think?
dlg.tilda.hours.1.why: the two-note bell as the measure

dlg.tilda.hours.r0.text: Staying. ...Say it once more, slower. I'd like it on the slate in your handwriting.
dlg.tilda.hours.r0.why: she wants it recorded, the closest she gets to tears

dlg.tilda.hours.r1.text: Together. Now that's a plan I'd stock. Bring ideas on Thursday. I'll bring the tea.
dlg.tilda.hours.r1.why: a day attached; her wish for someone to sit for tea

dlg.tilda.hours.r2.text: Gently. Recounting with kindness. I'll try it. The cat can check my sums.
dlg.tilda.hours.r2.why: takes the joke, keeps the cat

event.tilda_heart6.after.text: Said out loud, it weighs less. Turn the sign back, would you? And not a word to Felix. He'd worry, then bring fish.
event.tilda_heart6.after.why: no thank-you; she closes the confession with a fond joke

event.tilda_heart8.intro.text: Stocktake day. Help me shift the flour? There's a tin behind that shelf I've been not looking at for years.

dlg.tilda.card.1.text: My mother's pumpkin pie. The only thing she ever wrote down. I've never baked it. What if I get it wrong?

dlg.tilda.card.c0.text: Bake it. I'll stand right there.

dlg.tilda.card.c2.text: Share it. The pie feud can cope.

dlg.tilda.card.r0.text: Bake it. Yes. With you by the oven, so I can't back out.

dlg.tilda.card.r2.text: The whole village. ...The pie feud will be livid. I love it.

event.tilda_heart8.after.text: {if choice:card.bake}Flour, butter, and her handwriting. Saturday, before opening. Don't be late, or I'll lose my nerve.{else}{if choice:card.keep}Safe, then. A card doesn't need to be a pie to matter. Back in the tin.{else}Sharing it, then. A copy for every kitchen. Mother would have scolded me, then smiled.{/if}{/if}
event.tilda_heart8.after.why: each choice settles; bake gets a day

event.tilda_heart10.intro.text: Close your eyes. No, really. I've done something to the front of the shop and I can't watch you see it.

event.tilda_heart10.give.text: From her card, the very first one. Take it. And yes, that's your farm on my sign. Supplier. In paint, not chalk.
event.tilda_heart10.give.why: the pie and the sign; paint means permanent

event.tilda_heart10.thanks.text: {if choice:card.share}I copied the recipe for every kitchen, and put your name at the bottom. In chalk, so it can grow.{else}{if choice:card.bake}The pie came out right. It tasted like June, and my mother, and you.{else}The card's still in its tin. The pie's yours. Both are the best stock I've got.{/if}{/if}
event.tilda_heart10.thanks.why: each branch closes the card arc

event.tilda_friend.ask.text: Saturday stocktake, and the window's three sunflowers short of finished. Have you any?

event.tilda_friend.fallback.text: Three sunflowers, if you find them. The window's half dressed and mortified.

event.tilda_friend.success.text: Three sunflowers! The window looks like noon. You're on the slate, under 'saved the display.'

event.tilda_birthday.intro.text: It's my birthday. I don't make a fuss, I make a large pie. Come in, and whatever you do, don't read the slate.
event.tilda_birthday.intro.why: invites the very thing she forbids

dlg.tilda.birthday.r0.text: Oh. Well. That goes at the top of the slate, in capitals, where I'll see it every morning.
dlg.tilda.birthday.r0.why: she records instead of saying thank you

dlg.tilda.birthday.r1.text: A flower, in my shop! It goes in the window, beside the good pumpkin.

dlg.tilda.birthday.r2.text: You'd mind it? That's the best present. Take the stool. The cat bites coins, not customers.

event.tilda_birthday.after.text: {if choice:bday.tilda.wish}Capitals, on the slate. It reads very well from the street.{else}{if choice:bday.tilda.flower}The flower's in the window. Half the village asked who sent it. I said an account in good standing.{else}An hour off! I read a whole chapter upstairs. The shop survived. I'm slightly offended.{/if}{/if}
event.tilda_birthday.after.why: each branch ends on its funniest word

event.overheard_tilda_felix_1.l1.text: Felix. Your carp is eight coins today. On Monday it was six.

event.overheard_tilda_felix_1.l3.text: It's been in a bucket since dawn. It hasn't grown. Your prices have.

event.overheard_tilda_felix_2.l2.text: I remember the winter you fell in. And the Tuesday you fell in again.

event.overheard_tilda_felix_2.l4.text: Soup, a blanket, and 'Thin Ice' on the slate in capitals. You walked straight past it.

event.overheard_tilda_felix_3.l2.text: Oh, Felix. A very good fish. It stays up until the thaw.
event.overheard_tilda_felix_3.l2.why: she keeps his entry despite hating fish

event.overheard_tilda_felix_3.l4.text: The pond always knows. Sit down, Felix. I've made tea for two again.
event.overheard_tilda_felix_3.l4.why: her wish for someone to sit for tea

event.overheard_tilda_felix_4.l2.text: I'll judge it kindly, Felix. Then I'll salt it.
event.overheard_tilda_felix_4.l2.why: the verdict Felix calls a sentence

event.overheard_tilda_felix_4.l4.text: To old friends, dear. The crust is mine. The fish goes to the cat.
event.overheard_tilda_felix_4.l4.why: toast; her one 'dear' in this batch

event.overheard_tilda_wren_1.l1.text: Wren. Your chalkboard looks remarkably like my slate.

event.overheard_tilda_wren_1.l3.text: Flattery earns a ribbon. Imitation earns a bill.
event.overheard_tilda_wren_1.l3.why: shop logic, sets up Wren's 'A ribbon!'

event.overheard_tilda_wren_2.l1.text: I've heard something. About a certain cat, and a certain windowsill.

event.overheard_tilda_wren_2.l3.text: Then we'll trade. Yours first. I have a reputation to protect.

event.overheard_tilda_wren_3.l1.text: Six days at that counter this week. Save me a seat later?

event.overheard_tilda_wren_3.l3.text: One cup. Then back to the slate.
event.overheard_tilda_wren_3.l3.why: sets up Wren's 'The slate will wait'

event.overheard_tilda_juno_1.l2.text: Three clasps is two months of bread. The hinge is a tip. I'll put it on the slate.

event.overheard_tilda_juno_1.l4.text: The smiley face is priceless. That's why I can't charge for it.

event.overheard_tilda_juno_2.l1.text: You've grown, Juno. You used to stand under the jar of hooks and glare at it.

event.overheard_tilda_juno_2.l3.text: I know. I moved the sack there the week you started.

event.overheard_tilda_juno_3.l2.text: Open one in Wetherell and I'll stock your first shelf. Go farther, and I'll post you pie.
event.overheard_tilda_juno_3.l2.why: support either way; the shop does not stock anvils

event.overheard_tilda_juno_3.l4.text: Good. This street could use more noise.
event.overheard_tilda_juno_3.l4.why: her fear of a shrinking village, answered

event.overheard_tilda_bram_1.l1.text: Bram. There's a pie crust on your bench. For the hinges, the lamp, and the shelf.
event.overheard_tilda_bram_1.l1.why: her thanks in goods, not words

event.overheard_tilda_bram_1.l3.text: You never say thank you. I never say you're welcome. That's how the slate stays even.
event.overheard_tilda_bram_1.l3.why: their arrangement, Bram gets the last word

adds.text: Nobody sits in a shop. They lean, they pay, the bell goes twice. You sat.
adds.why: her real want (a customer who sits) said sideways

adds.text: Same chair on Thursday? I'll bake fewer scones. That's a lie, but a polite one.
adds.why: ends on a promise with a day attached

adds.text: She wrote down one recipe in her whole life. I know roughly where it is. I haven't looked.
adds.why: plants the recipe card for heart 8; ends the scene

threads.tilda_heart5: Whether the player comes back Thursday, and who else Tilda keeps baking extra for.
threads.tilda_heart2: Where the one recipe Tilda's mother wrote down is, and why Tilda has never looked.
threads.story_notes_tilda: Which two doors get Tilda's next notes today.
threads.story_scarecrows: Next fall's rematch, and what Tilda will add to her scarecrow.
threads.tilda_heart4: What the rest of the slate says about everyone else.
threads.tilda_heart6: Whether the bell rings more often, and what the player brings on Thursday.
threads.tilda_heart8: What Tilda does with her mother's card, and whether she finally bakes from it.
threads.tilda_heart10: The farm is on the sign now; what else the shop will stock from it.
threads.tilda_friend: What the window will need next Saturday.
threads.tilda_birthday: Who else will notice the slate's capitals, or the flower in the window.
threads.overheard_tilda_felix_2: What else from that long winter is still on the slate.
threads.overheard_tilda_felix_3: Who the second cup is usually for.
threads.overheard_tilda_felix_4: Whether the cat finishes the fish pie.
threads.overheard_tilda_juno_3: Whether Juno's forge ever opens next door to Bram.

notes: tilda_heart5: title says scones but the effect gives food.mashed_potato x2; I made line .2 name the mashed potato so text and item agree.
tilda_heart2: my added last line says her mother wrote down only one recipe; heart 8's card is it. The gratin was taught by hand, so no contradiction.
story_pumpkin_*: the closing line by Dorian/Marcus/Felix talks about the speaker in third person ('He's returning it...'); it reads like narration and should be [narration] or rewritten by them.
hall_dance: Wren says 'seven winters' of the roof pool; canon says six winters.
tilda_heart10: bible says she hands over the original two-note bell; the scene gives only the pie. I kept the item; the bell could be a later gift.
tilda_heart6: I removed 'every night' from her worry (persona: no talk of nights) and replaced the thank-you close.
overheard_tilda_wren_3: Wren says 'Come at six', but Tilda's schedule has her at the saloon from seven. I changed Tilda's 'tonight' to 'later'; Wren's 'six' should become 'seven'.
